newsitem.title: FRANCE: HORSE RACING-HEAD RETIRES WITH ONE LAST WIN.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-HEAD RETIRES WITH ONE LAST WIN.

text.p: Freddie Head, one of Europe's most successful jockeys with four Prix de L'Arc De Triomphe victories, retired on Tuesday after winning at Deauville on a horse trained by his sister.

"It was a symbolic way to go because not only was Marathon trained by my sister but he was wearing my grandfather's colours," said the 50-year-old Frenchman, who added that he felt he was losing half of his life by calling it a day.
"Of course I could have continued riding but you must know that the time to stop is when things are still going well."

Head, whose father Alec and grandfather Willie were also jockeys, had been associated with some great champions over the years, including Three Troikas, Lyphard and Miesque, and had a huge following in France.
He partnered the Stavros Niarchos-owned and Francois Boutin trained Miesque to victory in the 1,000 Guineas and the Breeders Cup Mile.
"I think that Miesque is the best filly I have ever ridden, but I don't think any horse anywhere could have beaten Three Troikas the day we won the Prix de L'Arc de Triomphe in 1979," Head said.
He rode more than 2,500 winners worldwide, taking his first win at Fontainebleau, France, in April 1964.
His tally of Arc winners remains a joint record.
